notes.summary: Reconciled test/specs/REQ-158.md against the real, shipped tests (it predated both the implementation and the rework's delimiter-injection regression tests, and still described the superseded raw-0x00/0x0A-separator hash scheme instead of the current length-prefixed framing). Verified all 7 of REQ-158's real acceptance_criteria (read directly from docs/requirements.yaml lines 7958-7966, not paraphrased) each have a specific failing test -- mapping table added to the spec's new final section. Ran active mutation testing against lib/letflow/engine/lua/manifest.ex as instructed and found one real gap, closed it.
mutation_testing: Mutation 1 -- hash-comparison always returns :ok (validate_at_load/3's `if computed_hash == registered_hash` replaced with `if true`): CAUGHT. mix test result before fix: 25/28 passed (3 failures) against the then-28-test baseline. Reverted, confirmed clean baseline restored (mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean).

Mutation 2 -- ordering: compute_hash/2 called before validate_shape/1 inside validate_at_load/3 (moved the hash computation ahead of the shape-error case clause): CAUGHT. mix test result: 27/28 passed (1 failure -- the shape-invalid-manifest short-circuit test, which fails with a FunctionClauseError from compute_hash/2's own is_binary(script_id) guard on the nil script_id fixture). Reverted, confirmed clean.

Mutation 3 -- length-prefix framing shrunk from 32-bit to 16-bit (<<byte_size(field)::32>> -> <<byte_size(field)::16>>): NOT CAUGHT by any pre-existing test. mix test result: 28/28 passed unchanged -- every determinism/sensitivity/collision test in the file only ever compares compute_hash/2 against itself on two different inputs, never against an independently-computed absolute value, so a systematic framing change that preserves all relative properties slips through undetected. GAP CLOSED: added a new test in manifest_test.exs, 'matches an independently-reconstructed digest over the documented byte layout', which reconstructs the expected SHA-256 input entirely independently (via :crypto.hash/2 directly, not calling any of Manifest's own helpers) per the moduledoc's documented 32-bit-length-prefixed, script_id-then-sorted-capabilities-then-script_source byte layout. Verified this new test: passes against real code (mix test manifest_test.exs -> 26 passed after adding it, before the other new doc-gap tests), and fails under both the 16-bit-prefix mutant (25/26 passed, the new test is the one failure) and a second mutant that reorders the three concatenated segments (25/26 passed, same test fails). Both mutants reverted and a clean mix compile --warnings-as-errors + mix test run confirmed after each revert.
notes.documentation_gap_fix: Added one sentence to lib/letflow/engine/lua/manifest.ex's moduledoc (top, before the INV-MAN-2 paragraph): 'A caller constructing a Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor.script_ref() value should prefer the map shape %{manifest: t(), script_source: binary()} ... rather than Executor's legacy bare-binary() shape, which exists only to keep ~40 pre-existing test call sites ... compiling and running unchanged.' Added the matching one-sentence steer inline to executor.ex's `@typedoc` for `script_ref`. Two new tests in manifest_test.exs assert both doc strings (moduledoc via Code.fetch_docs/1's module doc, and the script_ref type's own doc via the type_docs component of Code.fetch_docs/1) contain 'should prefer'/'legacy'/'manifest'.
notes.wall_clock_and_randomness: Confirmed no test in either file depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness. manifest_test.exs uses only fixed, literal test-authored values. manifest_executor_audit_test.exs uses Ecto.UUID.generate() for instance_id/actor_id -- used only to obtain unique identifiers, matching the existing lua_script_audit_test.exs convention, not as an input any assertion's pass/fail depends on being a particular value.
notes.test_isolation: manifest_test.exs: every function under test is pure (no Repo, no process state) -- async: true is correct and safe. manifest_executor_audit_test.exs: each test calls its own provisioned_tenant() helper independently (not shared via setup), which creates a uniquely-slugged Tenant + a real Postgres schema via TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 + replay_migrations/2, and registers an on_exit/1 that DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADEs and deletes the Registration/Tenant rows -- verified by reading the file in full. This mirrors test/letflow/engine/lua_script_audit_test.exs's established shape exactly. No cross-test leakage risk found.
